title: How do sticks tell us about missing cows?
description: In the Stone Age, a herd's sticks are matched one to one with its cows, and the leftover sticks answer the questions of missing cows and of a neighbour with more. Keeko's doubt is that the three spare sticks mean we have three more cows than the neighbour.
teaching_notes: One idea: matching each cow with one stick lets us count and compare without number names, and leftover sticks show who has more. Watch for students who read the spare sticks as belonging to the herd they are comparing from, when they lie in the other bundle.

video_script.why: The child sees that a one-to-one match with sticks answers how many are missing and who has more, before any number names exist.
video_script.substitution: Remove one stick for each cow that returns, then pair our bundle with the neighbour's and look at the sticks left over.
video_script.anchor: a herd of cows in the Stone Age, with a bundle of sticks, one stick for each cow, and the neighbour's bundle beside it
video_script.wrong_answer: we have three more cows than the neighbour
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko sees three unpaired sticks and says the herd has three more cows. The spare sticks lie in the neighbour's bundle, so the neighbour has more.
video_script.payoff_line: Two cows are missing, and we need three more to match the neighbour

final_answer.value: 2 cows are missing; fewer cows than the neighbour; 3 more cows needed
final_answer.spoken: two cows are missing, we have fewer cows than the neighbour, and three more cows are needed

hold_back: 2 cows are missing; fewer cows than the neighbour; 3 more cows needed
never_show: the answer card before the last beat of the board solution
maths_rules: the morning bundle has one stick for each cow, a one-to-one mapping between cows and sticks
each returning cow removes one stick, so each stick left stands for a cow that has not returned
pairing our morning bundle with the neighbour's bundle leaves 3 sticks unpaired, all in the neighbour's bundle
the neighbour has 3 more sticks than our bundle, so we have fewer cows and need 3 more to match
video_script.design: One idea: sticks matched one to one answer all three questions. The two bundles stay on the stage all video; sticks leave and pair up one step at a time.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the Stone Age.
<bookmark mark='herd'/>Around ten thousand years ago, we keep a herd of cows, and the herd is coming home.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>With no number names at all, how can we be sure that every cow has returned?

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

marks.name: the label one-to-one mapping appears on the lines
marks.next: the neighbour's bundle of sticks appears beside ours

narration: <bookmark mark='morning'/>In the morning, we keep one stick for each cow.
<bookmark mark='name'/>Giving each cow its own stick, with no two cows sharing a stick, is called a one-to-one mapping.
<bookmark mark='next'/>The neighbour keeps a bundle of sticks in the same way.

beats.on_screen: Given: one stick for each cow in the morning; one stick taken out for each returning cow; 2 sticks left; our bundle paired with the neighbour's leaves 3 sticks unpaired

marks.given: the facts are written as the given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, one stick for each cow in the morning. One stick comes out for each cow that returns. Two sticks are left.

beats.on_screen: To find: have all cows returned? Do we have fewer cows than the neighbour? How many more would we need?

marks.find: the words To find are written under the given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find whether all cows are back, and how our herd compares with the neighbour's.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: each returning cow removes exactly 1 stick, so every stick left stands for a cow that has not returned

marks.m1: a returning cow walks up and one stick leaves the bundle, one cow for one stick

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, take out sticks as the cows return.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Each returning cow removes exactly one stick. Each stick left stands for a cow that has not returned.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: sticks left = 2, so cows missing = 2

marks.m2: the 2 sticks left in the bundle are circled, each with a missing cow beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='s2'/>Step two, look at the sticks that are left.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Two sticks are left, so two cows are still missing.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: pair our morning bundle with the neighbour's bundle, one to one; 3 sticks have no partner, and they lie in the neighbour's bundle

marks.m3: lines pair our sticks with the neighbour's sticks, and 3 sticks of the neighbour's bundle stay without partners

narration: <bookmark mark='s3'/>Step three, pair our morning bundle with the neighbour's bundle, stick by stick.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Three sticks are left without partners, and all three lie in the neighbour's bundle.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: the neighbour has 3 more sticks than we have, so we have fewer cows; 3 more cows would make the herds equal

marks.m4: the 3 unpaired sticks are pulled across, and our bundle and the neighbour's bundle become the same length

narration: <bookmark mark='s4'/>Step four, read the unpaired sticks.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The neighbour has three sticks more, which means we have fewer cows. Three more cows would make the two herds equal.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 2 cows are missing; fewer cows than the neighbour; 3 more cows needed

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>Two cows are missing, and we need three more to match the neighbour.
<bookmark mark='res'/>Two cows are missing. We have fewer cows than the neighbour. Three more cows are needed.
